definition_zh: 合作的；协作的；共同完成的
definition_en: involving two or more people or groups that work together on a shared task
core_image: 几个人围着同一张桌子，把各自的笔迹写到一页纸上
scene: 项目组每周碰头，把各自负责的部分拼到一起。The team took a collaborative approach to the design.
sceneCN: 这里 collaborative 指「协作的」（第 1 个义项：多方共同参与的）；句意是团队在设计上采取了协作的方式。

pos.zh: 合作的；协作的；共同完成的

senses.title: Working together on a task
senses.definition: involving people or groups that work together on one shared task
senses.definitionCN: 由多方共同完成同一任务的
senses.example: The two schools ran a collaborative art show.
senses.exampleCN: 两所学校合办了一场艺术展。
senses.why: The Latin base meant working, and the prefix added the idea of together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为工作，前缀又加上了一起的含义。

senses.title: Designed for joint use
senses.definition: made so that several people can work on it at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 设计成可供多人同时使用的
senses.example: They opened a collaborative editing tool.
senses.exampleCN: 他们开放了一个协同编辑工具。
senses.why: Software extended the word from people to shared workspaces.
senses.whyCN: 软件把这个词从人扩展到共享的工作空间。

intro.en: Collaborative goes back to Latin laborare, to work, with the prefix com-, together.
intro.cn: collaborative 上溯拉丁语 laborare（工作），前缀 com- 表示一起。

items.en: Laborare meant to work or to toil.
items.cn: laborare 意为工作或劳作。

items.en: Collaborare joined com- with laborare to mean work together.
items.cn: collaborare 把 com- 与 laborare 结合，意为一起工作。

items.en: French collaboration named joint work, often in science.
items.cn: 法语 collaboration 指共同工作，常用于科学。

items.en: English adopted collaborate and soon formed collaborative.
items.cn: 英语先吸收 collaborate，很快又造出 collaborative。

items.en: The word now covers shared software and shared classrooms.
items.cn: 这个词如今涵盖共享软件与共享课堂。

note.en: The look-alike group holds adjectives and nouns built on similar Latin shapes, while the meaning group names what is shared and done together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是由相似拉丁形式构成的形容词与名词，近义组列出共同与共享。

entries.definition: willing to help and work with other people
entries.definitionCN: 愿意帮助他人并与他人合作的

entries.definition: relating to a large company
a person who works with another on a task
entries.definitionCN: 与他人共同完成一项任务的人

entries.definition: shared by two or more people or groups
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同拥有的

entries.definition: done by a group acting as a whole
entries.definitionCN: 由整体群体共同完成的

entries.definition: used or owned by more than one person
entries.definitionCN: 由不止一人使用或拥有的

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from the Latin root for work and the prefix for together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从拉丁语的工作词根与表示一起的前缀搭起这个词。

normal.en: Find labor inside the word: collaborative work is shared labour.
normal.cn: 词里藏着 labor：协作的工作就是分担的劳动。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, as in company and community.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，company 与 community 也是如此。

normal.en: The ending -ive makes it an adjective, a quality of a group.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 使它成为形容词，表示群体的一种性质。

normal.en: Collaborate is the verb, collaboration the noun, collaborative the adjective.
normal.cn: collaborate 是动词，collaboration 是名词，collaborative 是形容词。

normal.en: A collaborative tool lets several hands work on one page.
normal.cn: 协作工具让好几只手同时改同一页。

abstract.en: Picture four chairs pulled up to one wide table.
abstract.cn: 想象四把椅子围到一张宽桌旁。

abstract.en: Picture two hands holding the same pen above a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在同一张地图上方共握一支笔。

abstract.en: Picture a screen where three cursors move at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕上同时移动着三个光标。

examples.en: The report was a collaborative effort by three departments.
examples.cn: 这份报告是三个部门共同努力的成果。

examples.en: Students learn faster in a collaborative classroom.
examples.cn: 学生在协作式的课堂里学得更快。

examples.en: The app offers collaborative notes for small teams.
examples.cn: 这款应用为小团队提供协作笔记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collaborative 记成 com 加 labor：几个人一起干活，就是协作。

root: 源自拉丁语 laborare（工作）加前缀 com-（一起），经法语进入英语，指多方共同参与。

sensesIntro.en: From people sharing a task to tools that let many hands work on one page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从共同承担一项任务的人，到让多只手同改一页的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several people bent over one table, adding to the same page.
core.cn: 核心意象：几个人俯身同一张桌子，往同一页上添写。

branches.en: The human sense is the oldest: people working on one task.
branches.cn: 人的义项最古老：人们共同做一件事。

branches.en: The tool sense transfers the idea to shared software.
branches.cn: 工具义项把这个想法转移到共享软件上。

branches.en: Both senses depend on more than one participant.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖不止一个参与者。

branches.en: Shared labour is the literal meaning hidden in the Latin root.
branches.cn: 分担的劳动正是藏在拉丁词根里的字面义。

branches.en: A collaborative tool is only useful when others join in.
branches.cn: 协作工具只有在别人加入时才发挥作用。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin root labor, with com- for together and -ive for the adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词族建在拉丁词根 labor 上，com- 表一起，-ive 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Laborare, to work, is the living Latin base behind collaborate and laboratory.
latinIntro.cn: laborare（工作）是 collaborate 与 laboratory 背后活的拉丁词基。

items.meaning: to work together with others
items.example: The two labs collaborate on the vaccine.
items.exampleCN: 这两个实验室合作研发疫苗。

items.meaning: the act of working together
items.example: The book grew out of a long collaboration.
items.exampleCN: 这本书源于一次长期合作。

items.meaning: a person who works with another
items.example: Her main collaborator lives abroad.
items.exampleCN: 她的主要合作者住在国外。

items.meaning: in a way that involves working together
items.example: The students wrote the chapter collaboratively.
items.exampleCN: 学生们合作写成了这一章。

items.meaning: hard work or to work hard
items.example: The project took years of labor.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目花了数年的辛劳。

items.meaning: needing much time and effort
items.example: Copying the files by hand was laborious.
items.exampleCN: 手工抄写这些文件很费力。

items.meaning: to add details or to be very detailed
items.example: He refused to elaborate on the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他拒绝进一步说明这个计划。

items.meaning: a room used for scientific work
items.example: The samples were sent to the laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 样本被送到了实验室。

latinEntries.example: Latin collaborare joins com- with laborare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collaborare 由 com- 与 laborare 组合而成。

latinEntries.meaning: to work, toil or suffer effort
latinEntries.example: Laborare is the source of labour and laboratory.
latinEntries.exampleCN: laborare 是 labour 与 laboratory 的来源。

definition_en: to fall down suddenly, to fail completely, or to fall down because of illness or weakness
core_image: 一座楼在几秒之内塌成一堆瓦砾
scene: 旧仓库的屋顶在雨里撑不住了。The old roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
sceneCN: 这里 collapse 指「倒塌」（第 1 个义项：突然塌下）；句意是旧屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。

senses.title: Fall down suddenly
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of pressure or a loss of support
senses.definitionCN: 因压力或失去支撑而突然塌下
senses.example: The roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to fall together, which is exactly what a building does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为一起倒下，这正是一栋楼倒塌的样子。

senses.title: Fail completely
senses.definition: to fail suddenly and completely, as a system or a plan does
senses.definitionCN: 像制度或计划那样突然彻底失败
senses.example: The talks collapsed after two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈两小时后破裂了。
senses.why: An argument can fall down like a wall when its supports give way.
senses.whyCN: 论证的支撑一断，也会像墙一样倒下。

senses.title: Fall down from weakness
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of illness, injury or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 因病、受伤或疲劳突然倒下
senses.example: He collapsed at the end of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛终点倒下了。
senses.why: The body loses its support just as a structure does.
senses.whyCN: 身体像建筑物一样失去支撑。

intro.en: Collapse comes from Latin collabi, from com- together and labi, to slip or fall.
intro.cn: collapse 出自拉丁语 collabi，由 com-（一起）与 labi（滑落、倒下）组成。

items.en: Labi meant to slip, slide or fall.
items.cn: labi 意为滑、滑落或倒下。

items.en: Collabi described falling down in a heap.
items.cn: collabi 描述塌成一堆。

items.en: The participle collapsus was used of ruined buildings.
items.cn: 分词 collapsus 用于描述毁坏的建筑。

items.en: English collapse first described a building giving way.
items.cn: 英语 collapse 最初描述建筑垮塌。

items.en: Medicine and economics extended it to bodies and systems.
items.cn: 医学与经济学把它扩展到身体与制度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin-shaped words with similar endings, while the meaning group names ways of breaking down or losing strength.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾相似、带拉丁形态的词，近义组列出碎裂与失去支撑的说法。

entries.definition: to pass, as time does
to gather pages into the correct order
entries.definitionCN: 把书页按正确顺序整理

entries.definition: the hiding of the sun or moon by another body
entries.definitionCN: 太阳或月亮被另一天体遮住

entries.definition: to break into small pieces over time
to go down below a surface
to lose consciousness for a short time

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the Latin picture of falling together, then apply it to walls, plans and bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一起倒下的拉丁画面出发，再挪到墙、计划与身体上。

normal.en: Collapse hides the Latin verb labi, to slip, so the word pictures a slide downward.
normal.cn: collapse 里藏着拉丁动词 labi（滑落），画面就是往下滑。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, so everything falls at once.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，所以是所有东西同时倒下。

normal.en: A roof, a deal and a runner can all collapse in one second.
normal.cn: 屋顶、交易和奔跑者都可能在刹那间垮掉。

normal.en: Add -ible and collapsible means able to be folded down.
normal.cn: 加上 -ible，collapsible 就是能被折下来的。

normal.en: The noun keeps the same shape as the verb, so no ending is needed.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，不必另加词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a wall folding inward in a cloud of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙在尘土中向内折倒。

abstract.en: Picture a row of numbers on a screen suddenly turning blank.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的一排数字突然变成空白。

abstract.en: Picture a runner taking one more step and then folding to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑者又迈一步，然后蜷倒在地。

examples.en: The bridge collapsed during the storm.
examples.cn: 那座桥在暴风雨中坍塌了。

examples.en: The company collapsed after losing its main investor.
examples.cn: 这家公司在失去主要投资人后垮掉了。

examples.en: She collapsed with tiredness after the long flight.
examples.cn: 长途飞行后她累得倒下了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collapse 记成 com 加 lapse：所有东西一起滑落，就是塌掉。

root: 源自拉丁语 collabi，com-（一起）加 labi（滑落），本指建筑塌成一堆，后引申为制度失败与身体倒下。

sensesIntro.en: From a roof falling in to a plan breaking down, and then to a body that can no longer stand.
sensesIntro.cn: 从屋顶塌下，到计划破裂，再到再也站不住的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structure losing its support and folding into a heap.
core.cn: 核心意象：结构失去支撑，折成一堆。

branches.en: The building sense is the oldest and most physical.
branches.cn: 建筑义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: A plan fails the way a wall gives way.
branches.cn: 计划失败，就像墙失去支撑。

branches.en: The body sense borrows the same loss of support.
branches.cn: 身体义借用的同样是支撑的丧失。

branches.en: Both a roof and a person can fall in one sudden movement.
branches.cn: 屋顶和人都会在一个突然的动作中倒下。

branches.en: Systems and bodies both need support to keep standing.
branches.cn: 制度与身体都需要支撑才能立住。

intro.en: Collapse belongs to the Latin labi family, which also gives lapse, elapse and relapse.
intro.cn: collapse 属于拉丁语 labi 词族，这一族还给出 lapse、elapse 与 relapse。

latinIntro.en: The base labi, to slip, is the living element behind the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 labi（滑落）是整组词背后活的成分。

items.meaning: more than one collapse, or it falls down
items.example: The old wall collapses in heavy rain.
items.exampleCN: 这堵旧墙在大雨中塌下。

items.meaning: fell down or failed completely
items.example: The tent collapsed in the wind.
items.exampleCN: 帐篷在风里塌了。

items.meaning: falling down at this moment
items.example: They fled the collapsing building.
items.exampleCN: 他们逃离了正在倒塌的建筑。

items.meaning: able to be folded or pushed down
items.example: She carried a collapsible cup.
items.exampleCN: 她带着一只可折叠的杯子。

items.meaning: a small failure or a passing of time
items.example: A lapse in attention caused the error.
items.exampleCN: 一次走神造成了这个错误。

items.meaning: of time, to pass by
items.example: Three hours elapsed before the call came.
items.exampleCN: 三个小时过去，电话才来。

items.meaning: to fall back into illness or a bad habit
items.example: He relapsed after a week of rest.
items.exampleCN: 休息一周后他又复发了。

items.meaning: a body part slipping out of place
items.example: The doctor treated a minor prolapse.
items.exampleCN: 医生治疗了一处轻微的脱垂。

latinEntries.example: Latin collabi is built from com- and labi.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collabi 由 com- 与 labi 构成。

latinEntries.example: The verb labi also lies behind relapse.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 动词 labi 也藏在 relapse 背后。

definition_en: a person who works with you, especially in the same office or organization
core_image: 同一间办公室里抬头就能看见的那张熟悉面孔
scene: 早会开始前，几个人在茶水间低声交谈。She asked a colleague to check the numbers.
sceneCN: 这里 colleague 指「同事」（第 1 个义项：同一单位共事的人）；句意是她请一位同事核对数字。

derivatives.zh: 同僚之间互相支持的氛围

senses.title: Someone you work with
senses.definition: a person who works with you in the same office or organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一办公室或机构与你共事的人
senses.example: My colleague took the call while I was out.
senses.exampleCN: 我不在时我的同事接了电话。
senses.why: The Latin base meant one chosen together, a partner in a shared duty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为被一起选中的人，即共同承担职责的伙伴。

senses.title: A fellow member of a profession
senses.definition: a person who belongs to the same profession as you
senses.definitionCN: 与您属于同一职业的人
senses.example: She is a colleague from another university.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位来自另一所大学的同行。
senses.why: Scholars and doctors use it for equals beyond their own office.
senses.whyCN: 学者与医生用它指本单位之外的同行。

intro.en: Colleague comes from Latin collega, from com- together and legare, to choose or send.
intro.cn: colleague 出自拉丁语 collega，由 com-（一起）与 legare（选择、派遣）组成。

items.en: Legare meant to choose, send or appoint.
items.cn: legare 意为选择、派遣或任命。

items.en: Collega named a partner chosen to share an office.
items.cn: collega 指被选中共同任事的人。

items.en: French collègue carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 collègue 把词带向英语。

items.en: English colleague first meant a fellow official.
items.cn: 英语 colleague 最初指同僚官员。

items.en: The word spread to offices, schools and hospitals.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到办公室、学校与医院。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the colleg- shape, while the meaning group names people who work or stand beside you.
note.cn: 形近组收的是共享 colleg- 形态的词，近义组列出与你共事或同级的人。

entries.definition: a place where students study after school
entries.definitionCN: 学生毕业后继续求学的机构

entries.definition: friendly and equal among people at work
a group of teams or countries joined together
entries.definitionCN: 联合在一起的球队或国家

entries.definition: a person who works in the same place as you
entries.definitionCN: 与你同在一处工作的人

entries.definition: a person connected with your work
entries.definitionCN: 与你的工作有关联的人

entries.definition: a person of the same age, rank or ability
entries.definitionCN: 年龄、级别或能力相当的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks read the word as chosen together, then move from the same office to the same profession.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把它读成被一起选中，再从同一间办公室走到同一职业。

normal.en: Colleague and college share a beginning but not a meaning.
normal.cn: colleague 与 college 开头相同，意思却不同。

normal.en: Two colleagues are two people picked together for one job.
normal.cn: 两位同事就是为同一份工作被一起选中的两个人。

normal.en: The ending sounds like league, a group joined by a common aim.
normal.cn: 词尾听起来像 league，即因共同目标联合的群体。

normal.en: A colleague works beside you, a friend may not.
normal.cn: 同事在你身边工作，朋友却未必。

normal.en: The adjective collegial describes the friendly side of that relationship.
normal.cn: 形容词 collegial 描述这种关系中友善的一面。

abstract.en: Picture two desks facing each other under one lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象两张桌子在一盏灯下相对而放。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag on a door beside your own.
abstract.cn: 想象你门牌旁边的那块名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing a cup of tea across the aisle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一杯茶递过走道。

examples.en: I share an office with two colleagues.
examples.cn: 我和两位同事共用一间办公室。

examples.en: A colleague from the lab helped me finish the report.
examples.cn: 实验室的一位同事帮我完成了报告。

examples.en: She greeted her former colleagues at the conference.
examples.cn: 她在会议上问候了以前的同事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 colleague 记成 college 加 ague：同一所学院里一起做事的人，就是同事。

root: 源自拉丁语 collega，com-（一起）加 legare（选择、派遣），本指一起被任命共事的人。

sensesIntro.en: From the person at the next desk to the person in the same profession elsewhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 从隔壁桌的人，到身在别处却与你同行的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar face rising from the next desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：从隔壁桌抬起头来的那张熟悉面孔。

branches.en: The office sense is the everyday one today.
branches.cn: 办公室义是今天最日常的用法。

branches.en: The professional sense reaches beyond one workplace.
branches.cn: 职业义超出了单个工作场所。

branches.en: Both senses rest on shared work rather than friendship.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在共同工作上，而非友谊。

branches.en: A colleague is chosen into the same duty, not born into it.
branches.cn: 同事是被选来共担职责的，而不是天生的关系。

branches.en: Researchers call their equals colleagues across the world.
branches.cn: 研究者把世界各地的同行都称为 colleague。

intro.en: The family grows from the Latin root legare, with collegial and collegiate forming the adjective side.
intro.cn: 这个词族从拉丁词根 legare 生长，collegial 与 collegiate 构成形容词一侧。

latinIntro.en: Collega and legare are the Latin sources, and college keeps the same root in a different sense.
latinIntro.cn: collega 与 legare 是拉丁语来源，college 以另一义保留同一词根。

items.meaning: more than one person you work with
items.example: Her colleagues supported the new plan.
items.exampleCN: 她的同事们支持这项新计划。

items.meaning: the relationship between colleagues
items.example: Good colleagueship made the work lighter.
items.exampleCN: 良好的同事情谊让工作轻松了些。

items.meaning: friendly and equal among colleagues
items.example: The department kept a collegial tone.
items.exampleCN: 这个部门保持着同僚式的友好气氛。

items.meaning: the quality of mutual support among colleagues
items.meaningCN: 同僚间互相支持的特性
items.example: Meetings are run with real collegiality.
items.exampleCN: 会议在真正的同僚氛围中进行。

items.meaning: a body of people, now a place of study
items.meaningCN: 原指一群共事者，现指学院
items.example: He teaches at a small college.
items.exampleCN: 他在一所小学院教书。

items.meaning: relating to a college or its members
items.meaningCN: 与学院或其成员有关的
items.example: The team plays in a collegiate league.
items.exampleCN: 这支队伍参加大学联赛。

items.meaning: a group joined for a common purpose
items.meaningCN: 为共同目的联合的群体
items.example: The two towns formed a league.
items.exampleCN: 两个镇结成了一个联盟。

items.meaning: to give a duty to another person
items.example: A good manager knows how to delegate.
items.exampleCN: 好的管理者懂得如何分派任务。

latinEntries.meaning: a partner in office or duty
latinEntries.example: The Roman collega shared power for one year.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 罗马的同僚共同掌权一年。

latinEntries.example: Legare also gives English the word delegate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: legare 也为英语提供了 delegate 一词。

definition_en: to bring things of the same kind together, to go and get something, or to gather in a group
core_image: 把散落在各处的同类物件拢进一只盒子
scene: 孩子把地上的贝壳一枚枚捡进小桶。He collects stamps from every country he visits.
sceneCN: 这里 collect 指「收集」（第 1 个义项：把同类东西收起来）；句意是他收集他去过的每个国家的邮票。

senses.title: Bring things together
senses.definition: to bring things of the same kind together over time
senses.definitionCN: 长期把同类东西聚到一起
senses.example: She collects old maps of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她收集这座城市的旧地图。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to gather by choosing, so collecting is a series of choices.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为挑选着聚拢，所以收集是一连串选择。

senses.title: Go and get something
senses.definition: to go to a place and take something away
senses.definitionCN: 到某处把东西取走
senses.example: I will collect the tickets at the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 我会在服务台取票。
senses.why: Gathering also means walking to the place where the thing waits.
senses.whyCN: 聚拢也意味着走到物件等待的地方。

senses.title: Gather as a crowd
senses.definition: to come together in a group, as people do
senses.definitionCN: 像人群那样聚到一处
senses.example: A crowd collected outside the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在大厅外聚集起来。
senses.why: People gather the way objects do, so the verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 人聚拢的方式和物件一样，于是动词兼指两者。

intro.en: Collect comes from Latin colligere, from com- together and legere, to pick or read.
intro.cn: collect 出自拉丁语 colligere，由 com-（一起）与 legere（挑选、阅读）组成。

items.en: Legere meant to pick up, choose or read.
items.cn: legere 意为捡起、挑选或阅读。

items.en: Colligere meant to gather things into one place.
items.cn: colligere 意为把东西聚到一处。

items.en: French collecter carried the sense toward English.
items.cn: 法语 collecter 把这一含义带向英语。

items.en: English collect covered both objects and people.
items.cn: 英语 collect 同时涵盖物件与人。

items.en: It now also means to fetch something that waits for you.
items.cn: 它如今还指去取等候你的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group holds verbs built with lect, while the meaning group shades different ways of bringing things together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是含 lect 的动词，近义组细分几种聚拢的方式。

entries.definition: to choose one thing from several
to choose someone by voting
to join two things together
to bring people or things into one place
to increase in amount slowly over time
to bring parts or people together

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from picking things up one by one, then add fetching and crowding.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一件件捡起东西入手，再加上去取与聚拢。

normal.en: Collect and select share the Latin verb legere, to pick.
normal.cn: collect 与 select 共享拉丁动词 legere（挑选）。

normal.en: To collect is to pick many times, so the prefix com- adds them up.
normal.cn: 收集就是反复挑选，前缀 com- 把它们加在一起。

normal.en: The same verb covers stamps and parcels, because both are taken up.
normal.cn: 同一个动词既管邮票也管包裹，因为两者都是被取走。

normal.en: A crowd collects as coins collect in a box.
normal.cn: 人群聚拢，就像硬币被收进盒子。

normal.en: Collector keeps the -or ending of a person who acts.
normal.cn: collector 保留了表示施动者的 -or 词尾。

abstract.en: Picture hands moving shells from sand into a small bucket.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把贝壳从沙里捡进小桶。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk sliding a parcel across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象职员把包裹从柜台这边推过来。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd slowly closing around a street singer.
abstract.cn: 想象人群慢慢围住一位街头歌手。

examples.en: He collects coins from the countries he visits.
examples.cn: 他收集他去过的国家的硬币。

examples.en: Please collect your bags before leaving the train.
examples.cn: 下火车前请取走您的行李。

examples.en: Students collected in the yard after the bell.
examples.cn: 铃响之后学生们在院子里聚了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collect 记成 com 加 lect：把挑出来的东西一起收进盒子。

root: 源自拉丁语 colligere，com-（一起）加 legere（挑选、捡起），本指聚拢，后扩展到领取与人群聚集。

sensesIntro.en: From picking objects up to fetching what waits for you, and then to people coming together.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西捡起，到去取等候之物，再到人聚到一处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered things drawn into one container.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的东西被收进同一个容器。

branches.en: The gathering sense is the default meaning today.
branches.cn: 聚拢义是今天默认的含义。

branches.en: Fetching is gathering one waiting thing.
branches.cn: 领取就是聚拢一件等候你的东西。

branches.en: People collecting form a crowd without any object.
branches.cn: 人聚集时不涉及任何物件，只形成人群。

branches.en: Both take something into your hands from elsewhere.
branches.cn: 两者都是把别处的东西拿到手中。

branches.en: Objects and people both move toward one point.
branches.cn: 物件与人都是朝同一个点靠拢。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin root legere, with com- and -or and -ion forming the main branches.
intro.cn: 这个词族建在拉丁词根 legere 上，com-、-or 与 -ion 构成主要分支。

latinIntro.en: Legere, to pick or read, also stands behind select, elect and lecture.
latinIntro.cn: legere（挑选、阅读）也支撑着 select、elect 与 lecture。

items.meaning: brings things together or fetches them
items.example: She collects letters from the post box.
items.exampleCN: 她从邮筒里取信。

items.meaning: gathered together or fetched
items.example: The data were collected last spring.
items.exampleCN: 这些数据是去年春天收集的。

items.meaning: the activity of gathering things
items.example: Collecting stamps taught him patience.
items.exampleCN: 集邮教会了他耐心。

items.meaning: a person who collects things
items.example: A collector paid a high price for it.
items.exampleCN: 一位收藏家为它出了高价。

items.meaning: worth keeping in a collection
items.example: The old tickets are now collectable.
items.exampleCN: 这些旧票如今成了收藏品。

items.meaning: a group of things gathered together
items.example: His collection fills three shelves.
items.exampleCN: 他的收藏占满三层架子。

items.meaning: shared by a whole group
items.example: The decision was a collective one.
items.exampleCN: 这是集体的决定。

items.meaning: the belief that the group comes first
items.example: The village practised a mild collectivism.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄实行一种温和的集体主义。

latinEntries.example: Latin colligere joins com- with legere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 colligere 由 com- 与 legere 构成。

latinEntries.meaning: to pick up, choose or read
latinEntries.example: Legere also gives English the verb select.
latinEntries.exampleCN: legere 也为英语提供了动词 select。

definition_en: a group of similar things kept together, the act of collecting, or money gathered for a cause
core_image: 整面墙的玻璃柜里排着同一主题的藏品
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里摆着一排排旧怀表。The museum owns a large collection of clocks.
sceneCN: 这里 collection 指「收藏品」（第 1 个义项：成套藏品）；句意是博物馆拥有一大批钟表收藏。

senses.title: A set of similar things
senses.definition: a group of similar objects kept together, often over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年收集并放在一起的一批同类物件
senses.example: His collection fills three shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 他的收藏占满了三层架子。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of gathering into a thing you can see.
senses.whyCN: 名词把聚拢的动作变成一件看得见的东西。

senses.title: The act of collecting
senses.definition: the work of bringing things together
senses.definitionCN: 把东西聚拢起来的行为
senses.example: The collection of data took six months.
senses.exampleCN: 数据收集花了六个月。
senses.why: English often names an action with the same noun as its result.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用同一个名词兼指动作与其结果。

senses.title: Money gathered for a cause
senses.definition: money collected from many people for a special purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的向许多人募集的钱
senses.example: The class held a collection for the shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 全班为收容所举行了一次募捐。
senses.why: Coins are gathered in a box, so the gathering itself became the fund.
senses.whyCN: 硬币被收进盒子，于是这次收集本身就成了善款。

intro.en: Collection comes from Latin collectio, a gathering, from the verb colligere.
intro.cn: collection 出自拉丁语 collectio（聚集），源头是动词 colligere。

items.en: Colligere meant to gather things into one place.
items.cn: colligere 意为把东西聚到一处。

items.en: Collectio named the act and the result of gathering.
items.cn: collectio 兼指聚拢的动作与结果。

items.en: French collection kept both senses alive.
items.cn: 法语 collection 让两种含义都保留下来。

items.en: English used it for a set of writings and for money gathered.
items.cn: 英语用它指一部文集，也指募集的钱。

items.en: Museums made the word the standard label for a kept set.
items.cn: 博物馆让这个词成为成套藏品的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds nouns ending in the same sound, while the meaning group names gathered sets, stored records and given money.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾同音的名词，近义组列出成套之物、存档与捐款。

entries.definition: a change that makes something right
a link between two things or people
entries.definitionCN: 两物或两人之间的联系

entries.definition: a group chosen from a larger set
entries.definitionCN: 从更大范围中挑出的一组

entries.definition: a varied group of things of one kind
a store of records and documents
entries.definitionCN: 存放记录与文件的地方

entries.definition: money given to help a cause
entries.definitionCN: 为帮助某项事业而给的钱

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the -ion noun from a kept set to an action and then to a box of coins.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子沿着 -ion 名词，从成套藏品走到动作，再到一箱硬币。

normal.en: Collection is what you get after you collect for years.
normal.cn: collect 多年之后得到的东西，就是 collection。

normal.en: The ending -ion often turns a verb into a noun of action or result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ion 常把动词变成表示动作或结果的名词。

normal.en: The same word can mean the act and the objects, so context decides.
normal.cn: 同一个词可指动作也可指物件，靠语境分辨。

normal.en: A collection box turns small coins into a fund.
normal.cn: 募捐箱把小硬币变成一笔善款。

normal.en: A poem collection is simply poems gathered into one book.
normal.cn: 诗集不过是被收进一本书里的诗。

abstract.en: Picture a glass case filled with pocket watches, all ticking.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃柜装满怀表，全都在走。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook filling with numbers month after month.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记本一月月被数字填满。

abstract.en: Picture a tin box on a counter slowly filling with coins.
abstract.cn: 想象柜台上一只铁盒慢慢装满硬币。

examples.en: Her collection of postcards comes from thirty countries.
examples.cn: 她的明信片收藏来自三十个国家。

examples.en: The collection of samples must follow a strict method.
examples.cn: 样本的采集必须遵循严格的方法。

examples.en: A collection was made for the family after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾之后为这家人发起了一次募捐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collection 记成 collect 加 ion：收来的东西摆在一起，就是一套收藏。

root: 源自拉丁语 collectio，由 colligere（聚拢）派生，兼指收集的动作、成套藏品与募集的款项。

sensesIntro.en: One noun holds the kept set, the work of keeping it and the money gathered for others.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词兼指成套藏品、收集的工作与为他人募得的钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass case where one kind of thing is arranged in rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只玻璃柜里，同类物件排成行。

branches.en: The kept set is the sense museums made famous.
branches.cn: 成套藏品是博物馆让它出名的义项。

branches.en: The act sense names the work before the result exists.
branches.cn: 动作义指结果出现之前的那段工作。

branches.en: The money sense grew from coins gathered in one box.
branches.cn: 款项义从收进一只盒子的硬币生长出来。

branches.en: Result and action share one noun in English.
branches.cn: 结果与动作在英语里共用一个名词。

branches.en: Both describe a gathering, of objects or of money.
branches.cn: 两者都描述聚拢，只是聚的是物件或钱。

intro.en: The family grows with -or for people, -ible for worth and compounds such as collection box.
intro.cn: 这个词族靠 -or 表人、-ible 表值得，以及 collection box 这类复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Collectio and colligere are the Latin sources, built on legere, to pick.
latinIntro.cn: collectio 与 colligere 是拉丁语来源，建在 legere（挑选）之上。

items.meaning: more than one gathered set
items.example: The library holds several rare collections.
items.exampleCN: 这家图书馆藏有几套珍本。

items.meaning: a box for people to put money in
items.example: A collection box stood by the door.
items.exampleCN: 门边放着一只募捐箱。

items.meaning: a person who gathers a collection
items.example: The collector knew every item by name.
items.exampleCN: 这位收藏家能叫出每件东西的名字。

items.meaning: to bring things together
items.example: They collect old photographs.
items.exampleCN: 他们收集旧照片。

items.meaning: worth keeping as a collection
items.example: The cards became highly collectible.
items.exampleCN: 这些卡片变得极具收藏价值。

items.meaning: shared by a group
items.example: The land was collective property.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地是集体财产。

items.meaning: a system that puts the group first
items.meaningCN: 群体优先的制度或信念
items.example: The plan leaned toward collectivism.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划偏向集体主义。

items.meaning: the activity of gathering a collection
items.example: Collecting runs in their family.
items.exampleCN: 收集是他们家的传统。

latinEntries.meaning: a gathering or a gathered set
latinEntries.example: The Latin collectio came from colligere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collectio 来自 colligere。

latinEntries.example: Colligere is the source of collect.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colligere 是 collect 的来源。

definition_en: shared by or involving a whole group of people, or a group that owns and runs something together
core_image: 一群人同时举起手，做出同一个决定
scene: 会议结束时，所有人一起点头通过方案。The decision was a collective one, not a personal choice.
sceneCN: 这里 collective 指「集体的」（第 1 个义项：群体共同拥有的）；句意是这是集体的决定，而非个人的选择。

senses.title: Shared by a group
senses.definition: shared by or belonging to all members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 由群体全体成员共享或共有的
senses.example: The land is collective property.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地是集体财产。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the act of gathering into a quality of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ive 把聚拢的动作变成整体的性质。

senses.title: A group owning something together
senses.definition: a group of people who own and run something jointly
senses.definitionCN: 共同拥有并经营某事的群体
senses.example: The farmers formed a collective.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们成立了一个合作社。
senses.why: When people gather for a common good, the gathered group itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 当人们为共同利益聚在一起，聚成的群体本身也得了这个名字。

intro.en: Collective comes from Latin collectivus, from colligere, to gather.
intro.cn: collective 出自拉丁语 collectivus，源头是 colligere（聚拢）。

items.en: Colligere meant to gather into one place.
items.cn: colligere 意为聚到一处。

items.en: Collectivus described what belongs to a gathered whole.
items.cn: collectivus 描述属于聚成之整体的东西。

items.en: French collectif carried the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 法语 collectif 把这个形容词带向英语。

items.en: English collective first described shared duties.
items.cn: 英语 collective 最初描述共同的职责。

items.en: It also names farms and workplaces owned in common.
items.cn: 它还指共同拥有的农场与工作场所。

note.en: The look-alike group holds adjectives with similar endings, while the meaning group names what is held in common.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾相似的形容词，近义组列出共同拥有与共同参与。

entries.definition: worth keeping as part of a collection
meant to put something right
thinking carefully, or throwing back light
used or owned by more than one person
entries.definitionCN: 由不止一人使用或拥有的

entries.definition: done by two or more people together
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方一起完成的

entries.definition: belonging to a whole community

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from collect plus -ive, then split the shared quality from the group itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把它拆成 collect 加 -ive，再把共享性质与群体本身分开。

normal.en: Collect plus -ive gives the quality of a gathered whole.
normal.cn: collect 加 -ive，得到聚成整体所具有的性质。

normal.en: A collective decision needs more than one hand.
normal.cn: 集体的决定需要不止一只手。

normal.en: The noun form names the group, so a farm can be a collective.
normal.cn: 名词形式指这个群体，所以农场也能是一个集体。

normal.en: Collectively means everyone acting as one body.
normal.cn: collectively 意为所有人作为一个整体行动。

normal.en: Collectivism is the belief that the group comes first.
normal.cn: collectivism 是认为群体优先的信念。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every hand rises at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人在同一刻举起手。

abstract.en: Picture a field worked by many families who share the harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象许多家庭共同耕种一块地，分享收成。

abstract.en: Picture one long table where everyone writes the same letter.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，所有人一起写同一封信。

examples.en: The team made a collective decision to start again.
examples.cn: 团队做出了重新开始的集体决定。

examples.en: The village runs a collective that sells its own cheese.
examples.cn: 这个村子经营着一家出售自制奶酪的合作社。

examples.en: These memories are part of our collective past.
examples.cn: 这些记忆是我们共同过去的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collective 记成 collect 加 ive：把大家的意见收在一起，就是集体的。

root: 源自拉丁语 collectivus，由 colligere（聚拢）派生，先指聚成整体的性质，后指共同经营的群体。

sensesIntro.en: First a quality shared by a whole, then the whole group that owns something.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是整体共享的性质，再是共同拥有某物的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one decision made by many hands at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个由许多只手同时做出的决定。

branches.en: The adjective sense describes what the group holds in common.
branches.cn: 形容词义描述群体共同拥有的东西。

branches.en: The noun sense turns that group into an organisation.
branches.cn: 名词义把这个群体变成一个组织。

branches.en: The quality and the body share one Latin root.
branches.cn: 性质与群体共享同一个拉丁词根。

branches.en: Collective memory belongs to no single person.
branches.cn: 集体记忆不属于任何单独的个人。

branches.en: A collective is a group that acts like one owner.
branches.cn: 合作社就是像一个所有者那样行动的群体。

intro.en: The family adds -ism, -ist and -ly to the base, and compounds such as collective farm.
intro.cn: 这个词族在词基上加 -ism、-ist 与 -ly，并有 collective farm 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Collectivus and colligere are the Latin sources, built on legere, to pick.
latinIntro.cn: collectivus 与 colligere 是拉丁语来源，建在 legere（挑选）之上。

items.meaning: more than one cooperative group
items.example: Several collectives share the same market.
items.exampleCN: 几个合作社共用同一个市场。

items.meaning: as a group rather than as individuals
items.example: The staff collectively chose the name.
items.exampleCN: 全体员工共同选定了这个名字。

items.meaning: the belief that the group comes before the person
items.meaningCN: 认为群体先于个人的信念
items.example: The essay defended a mild collectivism.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章为一种温和的集体主义辩护。

items.meaning: believing in group ownership
items.example: He held collectivist views in economics.
items.exampleCN: 他在经济上持集体主义观点。

items.meaning: the state of being a group
items.example: The law treats them as a collectivity.
items.exampleCN: 法律把他们视为一个整体。

items.meaning: a farm owned and worked by a group
items.meaningCN: 由群体拥有并耕种的农场
items.example: The collective farm shared its tools.
items.exampleCN: 集体农场共用工具。

items.meaning: what a whole society remembers
items.meaningCN: 整个社会共同记住的东西
items.example: The war lives on in collective memory.
items.exampleCN: 那场战争留在集体记忆里。

items.meaning: to bring property under group ownership
items.example: The state moved to collectivize the land.
items.exampleCN: 国家着手把土地收归集体。

latinEntries.example: Collectivus comes from the verb colligere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: collectivus 来自动词 colligere。

latinEntries.example: Colligere is the base of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colligere 是整个词族的根基。

definition_en: a place where students study after school, especially one that gives degrees or trains for a job
core_image: 草坪尽头那排爬满常春藤的教学楼
scene: 开学那天，新生拖着箱子走进校门。She teaches history at a small college.
sceneCN: 这里 college 指「学院」（第 1 个义项：高等教育机构）；句意是她在一所小学院教历史。

senses.title: A place of higher study
senses.definition: a place where students study after secondary school
senses.definitionCN: 学生在中学之后继续求学的机构
senses.example: She is in her first year at college.
senses.exampleCN: 她上大学一年级。
senses.why: The Latin word first meant a body of people joined by a duty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词最初指因共同职责而结合的一群人。

senses.title: A part of a university
senses.definition: one of the separate schools that form a university
senses.definitionCN: 组成大学的独立学院之一
senses.example: He applied to the college of engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 他申请了工程学院。
senses.why: Universities divided into smaller bodies, and each kept the old name.
senses.whyCN: 大学分成较小的团体，每个团体都保留了旧名。

senses.title: A school for a special skill
senses.definition: a school that trains people for a particular job
senses.definitionCN: 为特定职业培训人才的学校
senses.example: She trained at a college of nursing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在护理专科学校受训。
senses.why: Training also gathers teachers and learners into one body.
senses.whyCN: 职业培训也把师生聚成同一个团体。

intro.en: College comes from Latin collegium, a body of people sharing a duty.
intro.cn: college 出自拉丁语 collegium，指共担职责的一群人。

items.en: Collega meant a partner in office.
items.cn: collega 指共同任职的伙伴。

items.en: Collegium named the whole body of such partners.
items.cn: collegium 指这些伙伴组成的整体。

items.en: French collège named a community of scholars.
items.cn: 法语 collège 指学者团体。

items.en: English college first meant a society of priests or students.
items.cn: 英语 college 最初指教士或学生的团体。

items.en: It now names schools, faculties and whole institutions.
items.cn: 它如今指学校、学部乃至整个机构。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in spelling, while the meaning group names institutions of study.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写相近的词，近义组列出各类教育机构。

entries.definition: a person who works with you
relating to a college or its students
entries.definitionCN: 与学院或其学生有关的

entries.definition: a small settlement in the countryside
an institution that gives degrees in many fields
entries.definitionCN: 在多个领域授予学位的机构

entries.definition: an organisation for study or research
entries.definitionCN: 从事教学或研究的机构

entries.definition: a school for a special subject or skill
entries.definitionCN: 教授专门学科或技能的学校

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a body of scholars to a campus, then to a faculty and a training school.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从学者团体走到校园，再到学部和职业学校。

normal.en: College and colleague share a root: one is the group, the other a member.
normal.cn: college 与 colleague 同根：一个是团体，一个是成员。

normal.en: The Latin collegium was a body of partners, not a building.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 collegium 指的是一群伙伴，而不是一栋楼。

normal.en: Go to college is a phrase without an article, unlike go to the college.
normal.cn: go to college 不加冠词，表示上大学这件事本身。

normal.en: A university can hold several colleges inside it.
normal.cn: 一所大学内部可以包含好几个学院。

normal.en: The adjective collegiate keeps the same idea of a shared body.
normal.cn: 形容词 collegiate 保留的仍是共同团体的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a stone gate with ivy and a path across a lawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一座爬满常春藤的石门，一条小路穿过草坪。

abstract.en: Picture a lecture hall filling with students at nine.
abstract.cn: 想象九点时讲堂里陆续坐满学生。

abstract.en: Picture a row of practised hands learning to hold a needle.
abstract.cn: 想象一排练习拿针的手，正在学习护理。

examples.en: He plans to go to college next year.
examples.cn: 他打算明年上大学。

examples.en: The college of law is across the square.
examples.cn: 法学院在广场对面。

examples.en: She studied design at a college of art.
examples.cn: 她在艺术学院学习设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 college 记成一群同事共用的院子：collega 是人，collegium 是院。

root: 源自拉丁语 collegium（共担职责的团体），由 collega（同僚）集合而成，后指学者团体与求学之所。

sensesIntro.en: A body of people first, then the place where they study, and finally the parts of a university.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是一群人，再是他们求学的场所，最后是大学的各个学院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone gate opening onto a lawn and a hall of study.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇石门通向草坪与讲堂。

branches.en: The general school sense is the everyday one.
branches.cn: 泛指学校的义项是最日常的用法。

branches.en: Inside a university the word names one faculty.
branches.cn: 在大学内部，这个词指一个学部。

branches.en: A training college teaches a trade rather than a degree subject.
branches.cn: 专科学校教的是手艺，而非学位课程。

branches.en: Both senses point to an organised body of teachers and learners.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指向有组织的师生团体。

branches.en: Study and training both happen inside the same old name.
branches.cn: 求学与职业训练都发生在同一个古老名字之下。

intro.en: The family keeps the Latin collegium and grows with -iate, -ial and -ian.
intro.cn: 这个词族保留拉丁语 collegium，靠 -iate、-ial 与 -ian 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Collegium, a body of colleagues, and collega, a partner, are the Latin sources.
latinIntro.cn: collegium（同僚团体）与 collega（伙伴）是拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: more than one college
items.example: Several colleges share one library.
items.exampleCN: 几所学院共用一座图书馆。

items.meaning: relating to a college
items.example: They met in a collegiate hall.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一座学院礼堂见面。

items.meaning: friendly among equals
items.example: The staff kept a collegial spirit.
items.exampleCN: 教职员保持着同僚精神。

items.meaning: a member of a college
items.example: Every collegian wore the same tie.
items.exampleCN: 每位学院成员都戴同样的领带。

items.meaning: a person who works with you
items.example: A colleague from the college called.
items.exampleCN: 学院的一位同事打来电话。

items.meaning: a body of people sharing a duty
items.example: The Latin collegium met as one body.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collegium 作为一个整体集会。

items.meaning: planning to go to college
items.example: The program helps college-bound students.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目帮助准备上大学的学生。

items.meaning: a local college with shorter courses
items.example: He took evening classes at a community college.
items.exampleCN: 他在社区学院上夜课。

latinEntries.meaning: a body of colleagues or officials
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同僚或官员组成的团体
latinEntries.example: Collegium is the direct source of college.
latinEntries.exampleCN: collegium 是 college 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Collega gave English the word colleague.
latinEntries.exampleCN: collega 为英语提供了 colleague。

definition_en: an accident in which two moving objects hit each other, or a serious disagreement between ideas or people
core_image: 两辆车在路口来不及刹车的那一瞬
scene: 雨夜的路口，一辆货车突然转向。Two cars were badly damaged in the collision.
sceneCN: 这里 collision 指「碰撞」（第 1 个义项：两物相撞）；句意是两辆车在碰撞中严重受损。

senses.title: Two objects hitting
senses.definition: an accident in which two moving objects hit each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个运动物体互相撞上的事故
senses.example: The collision broke the front of the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞撞坏了卡车的前部。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to strike together, and the noun names that single moment.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为撞到一起，名词命名的就是那一瞬。

senses.title: A clash of ideas or interests
senses.definition: a serious disagreement between people, ideas or interests
senses.definitionCN: 人、观念或利益之间的严重冲突
senses.example: A collision of opinions delayed the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 意见冲突使表决推迟。
senses.why: Two arguments can strike like two vehicles when neither will turn.
senses.whyCN: 两种主张各不相让，就会像两辆车一样撞上。

intro.en: Collision comes from Latin collisio, from com- together and laedere, to strike.
intro.cn: collision 出自拉丁语 collisio，由 com-（一起）与 laedere（撞击）组成。

items.en: Laedere meant to strike or injure.
items.cn: laedere 意为撞击或伤害。

items.en: Collidere meant to strike two things together.
items.cn: collidere 意为把两物撞在一起。

items.en: Collisio named the striking itself.
items.cn: collisio 指撞击这件事。

items.en: French collision brought the noun into English.
items.cn: 法语 collision 把这个名词带进英语。

items.en: The word now also covers clashes of ideas.
items.cn: 这个词如今也涵盖观念冲突。

note.en: The look-alike group holds nouns ending in the same sound, while the meaning group names hits and disagreements.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾同音的名词，近义组列出撞击与分歧。

entries.definition: secret cooperation for a dishonest purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为不正当目的暗中串通

entries.definition: a choice that has been made
the act of splitting something into parts
a violent hit involving vehicles
the force of one object hitting another
entries.definitionCN: 一物撞击另一物的力量

entries.definition: a serious disagreement or struggle

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold the picture of two moving bodies meeting, then transfer it to ideas.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子抓住两个运动物相撞的画面，再把它挪到观念上。

normal.en: Collision hides collide, the verb that names the act.
normal.cn: collision 里藏着动词 collide，动作就由它命名。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, so two things arrive at one point.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，所以两样东西到了同一点。

normal.en: The ending -sion often marks a noun of action, like decision.
normal.cn: 词尾 -sion 常标示动作名词，例如 decision。

normal.en: Cars, ships and aircraft can all be in collision.
normal.cn: 汽车、船只和飞机都可能发生碰撞。

normal.en: When two opinions refuse to turn, that is also a collision.
normal.cn: 两种意见都不肯转向时，那也是一种冲突。

abstract.en: Picture two bright headlights closing on one narrow bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象两束车灯在同一座窄桥上逼近。

abstract.en: Picture a scatter of glass on wet asphalt.
abstract.cn: 想象湿沥青上散落着碎玻璃。

abstract.en: Picture two people rising at a meeting, both refusing to yield.
abstract.cn: 想象会上两人同时起身，谁都不肯让步。

examples.en: The collision happened at a quiet crossroads.
examples.cn: 碰撞发生在一个安静的路口。

examples.en: Helmets reduce the damage of a collision.
examples.cn: 头盔能减轻碰撞造成的伤害。

examples.en: A collision between duty and desire kept him awake.
examples.cn: 责任与欲望的冲突让他睡不着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collision 记成 collide 加 sion：两物撞到同一点，就是碰撞。

root: 源自拉丁语 collisio，由 collidere（撞到一起）派生，com- 表一起，laedere 表撞击。

sensesIntro.en: From metal meeting metal on a road to two firm opinions meeting in a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 从路上金属撞金属，到屋里两种坚决的意见相撞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths crossing at the same point at the same second.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路线在同一秒交于同一点。

branches.en: The physical sense is the oldest and most concrete.
branches.cn: 物理碰撞义最古老也最具体。

branches.en: The abstract sense keeps the same picture of two forces meeting.
branches.cn: 抽象义保留的仍是两种力量相遇的画面。

branches.en: Both senses need two parties and no room to turn.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要两方且无处可让。

branches.en: Insurance reports use the word for any vehicle hit.
branches.cn: 保险报告用这个词指任何车辆撞击。

branches.en: A collision of interests can stop a whole project.
branches.cn: 利益冲突能让整个项目停摆。

intro.en: The family is built on collide, with -sion for the event and -er for the machine.
intro.cn: 这个词族建在 collide 上，-sion 表事件，-er 表机器。

latinIntro.en: Collidere and laedere are the Latin sources of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: collidere 与 laedere 是整组词的拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: more than one crash or clash
items.example: Most collisions happen close to home.
items.exampleCN: 多数碰撞发生在离家不远的地方。

items.meaning: to hit something while moving
items.example: The two ships collided in fog.
items.exampleCN: 两艘船在雾中相撞。

items.meaning: hit another moving thing
items.example: The van collided with a bus.
items.exampleCN: 货车撞上了一辆公交车。

items.meaning: hitting each other at this moment
items.example: Two streams of air were colliding.
items.exampleCN: 两股气流正在相撞。

items.meaning: a machine that makes particles collide
items.example: The collider runs in a long tunnel.
items.exampleCN: 这台对撞机在一条长隧道中运行。

items.meaning: relating to a collision
items.example: They measured collisional energy.
items.exampleCN: 他们测量了碰撞能量。

items.meaning: a crash in which fronts meet
items.example: A head-on collision closed the road.
items.exampleCN: 一场正面相撞封闭了道路。

items.meaning: a crash between two aircraft in flight
items.meaningCN: 两架飞行器在空中相撞
items.example: The report studied the mid-air collision.
items.exampleCN: 报告研究了这起空中相撞。

latinEntries.example: Collidere is the verb behind collision.
latinEntries.exampleCN: collidere 是 collision 背后的动词。

latinEntries.example: Laedere supplies the second half of collidere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: laedere 提供了 collidere 的后半部分。

definition_en: a country or area controlled by another country, a group of people living together, or a group of the same animals or plants in one place
core_image: 远方土地上，一批外来者建起的整齐定居点
scene: 海边的礁石上密密麻麻爬满了同类的小生物。A colony of ants moved across the kitchen floor.
sceneCN: 这里 colony 指「聚居群体」（第 2 个义项：同类聚在一处）；句意是一群蚂蚁爬过厨房地面。

pos.zh: 殖民地；聚居群体；生物群落

senses.title: A controlled territory
senses.definition: a country or area ruled by another country that settled there
senses.definitionCN: 由他国统治并在那里定居的地区
senses.example: The island was once a colony.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛曾是殖民地。
senses.why: The Latin word named a settlement of farmers far from home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本指远离家乡的农人定居点。

senses.title: A group living together
senses.definition: a group of people of one kind living in the same place
senses.definitionCN: 同类人聚居在同一地方形成的群体
senses.example: A colony of painters took over the old street.
senses.exampleCN: 一群画家占据了那条老街。
senses.why: Any settlement of like people kept the old farming image.
senses.whyCN: 任何同类人的聚居都沿用了旧日农耕定居的画面。

senses.title: A group of organisms
senses.definition: a group of the same kind of animals or plants living in one area
senses.definitionCN: 同一类动植物生活在同一区域的群体
senses.example: The reef supports a large colony of crabs.
senses.exampleCN: 这片礁石养活了一个很大的蟹群。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the word because ants settle like farmers.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词，因为蚂蚁像农夫一样定居。

intro.en: Colony comes from Latin colonia, a settlement of farmers, from colere, to cultivate.
intro.cn: colony 出自拉丁语 colonia（农人定居点），源头是 colere（耕作）。

items.en: Colere meant to till the soil and to dwell.
items.cn: colere 意为耕作土地与居住。

items.en: Colonus was a farmer who worked the land.
items.cn: colonus 是耕种土地的农人。

items.en: Colonia named a settlement of such farmers abroad.
items.cn: colonia 指这类农人在外建立的定居点。

items.en: English colony described overseas settlements.
items.cn: 英语 colony 描述海外定居点。

items.en: Science applied it to groups of animals and plants.
items.cn: 科学把它用于动植物群体。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the spelling, while the meaning group names settlements, land and living groups.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写相近的词，近义组列出定居点、土地与聚居群体。

entries.definition: a light perfume named after a German city
entries.definitionCN: 以德国城市命名的淡香水

entries.definition: a high rank in the army
a tall stone post or a regular newspaper piece
entries.definitionCN: 高石柱或报纸的定期专栏

entries.definition: a place where people have made their home
land under the control of a state
a group of people living in one place
entries.definitionCN: 共同生活在一处的群体

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with farmers settling new land, then widen to any group that lives together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从农人开垦新地开始，再扩展到任何聚居的群体。

normal.en: Colony hides the Latin colere, to cultivate the soil.
normal.cn: colony 里藏着拉丁语 colere（耕作土地）。

normal.en: A colony began as farmers' fields, not as a government office.
normal.cn: 殖民地最初是一片农田，而不是一间衙门。

normal.en: Ants build a colony in the same way farmers build a village.
normal.cn: 蚂蚁建立群落，就像农人建立村庄。

normal.en: Colonial is the adjective, colonist the person, colonize the act.
normal.cn: colonial 是形容词，colonist 是人，colonize 是动作。

normal.en: The plural colonies changes y into ies.
normal.cn: 复数 colonies 把词尾 y 变成 ies。

abstract.en: Picture a neat row of new houses on an empty coast.
abstract.cn: 想象空旷海岸上一排整齐的新房。

abstract.en: Picture a street where every window shows a painter at work.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，每扇窗里都有画家在工作。

abstract.en: Picture a stone alive with hundreds of small shells.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头上爬满数百只小贝壳。

examples.en: The country gained independence from its former colony.
examples.cn: 这个国家从它的前殖民地获得了独立。

examples.en: An ant colony can build a city under a stone.
examples.cn: 一个蚁群能在石头下建起一座城。

examples.en: A colony of gulls nested on the far rocks.
examples.cn: 一群海鸥在远处的礁石上筑巢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 colony 记成 colere 开垦出来的地方：先是一片田，后来是一群人。

root: 源自拉丁语 colonia（农人定居点），由 colere（耕作、居住）派生，后指殖民地、聚居群体与生物群落。

sensesIntro.en: From tilled fields abroad to any group of people or creatures living in one place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从海外开垦的田地，到任何在一处生活的同类人或生物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young settlement of newcomers on distant soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：在远方土地上由新来者建立的定居点。

branches.en: The political sense grew from overseas farming settlements.
branches.cn: 政治义从海外农耕定居点生长出来。

branches.en: Any like-minded group living together can be a colony.
branches.cn: 任何志趣相投、聚居一处的群体都可称 colony。

branches.en: Biology borrows the word for ants, bees and seabirds.
branches.cn: 生物学借这个词指蚂蚁、蜜蜂与海鸟。

branches.en: Both senses describe people gathered in a new place.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述人聚在新地方。

branches.en: People and animals both settle in groups of their own kind.
branches.cn: 人与动物都会按同类聚成群体定居。

intro.en: The family grows from the root colere, with -ial, -ist and -ize forming its main words.
intro.cn: 这个词族从词根 colere 生长，-ial、-ist 与 -ize 构成主要成员。

latinIntro.en: Colonia and colere are the Latin sources, and culture shares the same root.
latinIntro.cn: colonia 与 colere 是拉丁语来源，culture 也共享同一词根。

items.meaning: more than one colony
items.meaningCN: 多块殖民地或多个群落
items.example: The bird colonies line the northern cliffs.
items.exampleCN: 鸟群沿北面的悬崖分布。

items.meaning: relating to a colony or its ruler
items.meaningCN: 与殖民地或其统治者有关的
items.example: The town keeps its colonial houses.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子保留着殖民地时期的房屋。

items.meaning: a person who settles in a new colony
items.example: Each colonist received a plot of land.
items.exampleCN: 每位定居者分到一块土地。

items.meaning: to settle and control a new area
items.meaningCN: 在新的地区定居并控制它
items.example: Birds colonize the island every spring.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类每年春天到这个岛上定居。

items.meaning: settled and controlled by outsiders
items.meaningCN: 被外来者定居并控制的
items.example: The coast was colonized long ago.
items.exampleCN: 这片海岸很久以前就被殖民了。

items.meaning: the process of settling a new area
items.example: The book studies the colonization of the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这本书研究该山谷的殖民过程。

items.meaning: the practice of ruling other lands
items.example: The museum examines the history of colonialism.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆审视殖民主义的历史。

items.meaning: supporting the rule of other lands
items.example: The old maps carry a colonialist view.
items.exampleCN: 那些旧地图带有殖民者视角。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 农人在外建立的定居点
latinEntries.example: Colonia is the direct source of colony.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colonia 是 colony 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Colere also lies behind the word culture.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colere 也藏在 culture 一词背后。

definition_en: the quality that makes things look red, blue or green, to put colour on something, or the natural tone of a person's skin
core_image: 一整排颜料管挤出的鲜艳色带
scene: 孩子把调色盘上的每一种颜料都试了一遍。She chose a warm yellow colour for the curtains.
sceneCN: 这里 colour 指「颜色」（第 1 个义项：视觉上的色彩）；句意是她为窗帘选了一种温暖的黄色。

senses.title: The quality of light
senses.definition: the quality that makes something look red, blue, green and so on
senses.definitionCN: 使物体看起来呈红、蓝、绿等的性质
senses.example: The sky changed colour at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时天空变了颜色。
senses.why: The Latin word first meant a covering, then the surface look of things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词最初指覆盖物，后指物体表面的样子。

senses.title: To add colour
senses.definition: to put colour on something or change its colour
senses.definitionCN: 给某物上色或改变它的颜色
senses.example: The children coloured the map with pencils.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用彩笔给地图上色。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to give a surface its colour.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：给表面以颜色。

senses.title: Skin tone
senses.definition: the natural tone of a person's skin
senses.definitionCN: 人皮肤天生的色调
senses.example: People of every colour joined the march.
senses.exampleCN: 各种肤色的人都参加了游行。
senses.why: Skin is the surface we see, so its tone is simply our colour.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤是我们看见的表面，它的色调自然就是我们的颜色。

intro.en: Colour comes through Old French from Latin color, a covering or an outward look.
intro.cn: colour 经古法语上溯拉丁语 color，指覆盖物或外表。

items.en: Color meant the surface look of a thing.
items.cn: color 指物体的表面样子。

items.en: The verb colare meant to cover or hide.
items.cn: 动词 colare 意为覆盖或遮蔽。

items.en: Old French colour kept both the noun and the verb.
items.cn: 古法语 colour 同时保留名词与动词。

items.en: English colour named hue and also outward appearance.
items.cn: 英语 colour 既指色调也指外观。

items.en: American spelling dropped the u, giving color.
items.cn: 美式拼写去掉 u，写作 color。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that sound close to colour, while the meaning group names shades and tints.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音接近 colour 的词，近义组列出各种色调。

entries.definition: the part of a shirt that goes around the neck
a high rank in the army
a person who makes a telephone call or visits
a particular shade of colour
a slightly different form of a colour
entries.definitionCN: 同一种颜色的细微变体

entries.definition: a pale or slight colour

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a layer laid over a surface, then move to paint and to skin.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从覆盖在表面上的一层出发，再走到颜料与皮肤。

normal.en: The Latin base meant a covering, so colour is what covers a surface.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基意为覆盖，所以颜色就是盖在表面上的东西。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the u that American English drops.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留了美式去掉的那个 u。

normal.en: The verb is simply the noun put to work.
normal.cn: 动词不过是名词被派去干活。

normal.en: Colourful adds -ful, meaning full of colour.
normal.cn: colourful 加 -ful，意为充满颜色。

normal.en: Skin colour is the same word because skin is the surface we see.
normal.cn: 肤色用同一个词，因为皮肤就是我们看见的表面。

abstract.en: Picture a row of paint tubes squeezed onto a glass palette.
abstract.cn: 想象一排颜料管挤在玻璃调色盘上。

abstract.en: Picture a child filling a grey drawing with red and blue.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子用红色和蓝色填满一幅灰线画。

abstract.en: Picture a sunset turning the whole river orange.
abstract.cn: 想象日落把整条河染成橘色。

examples.en: Blue is her favourite colour.
examples.cn: 蓝色是她最喜欢的颜色。

examples.en: He coloured the sky in his picture dark grey.
examples.cn: 他把画里的天空涂成了深灰色。

examples.en: The leaves change colour in late autumn.
examples.cn: 深秋时树叶会变色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 colour 记成盖在表面的一层色：涂上去是颜色，留在皮肤上是肤色。

root: 源自拉丁语 color（外表、颜色），与 colare（覆盖）相关，经古法语进入英语，美式拼作 color。

sensesIntro.en: A surface quality first, then the act of adding it, and finally the colour of skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是表面的性质，再是添加它的动作，最后是皮肤的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright band of paint laid across a pale surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道鲜亮的颜料铺在浅色表面上。

branches.en: The hue sense is the everyday meaning of the noun.
branches.cn: 色调义是名词最日常的含义。

branches.en: The verb names the act of laying colour on.
branches.cn: 动词义指把颜色铺上去的动作。

branches.en: Skin tone is the same quality seen on a person.
branches.cn: 肤色就是同一种性质在人身上的呈现。

branches.en: The noun and the verb share one shape, so one image serves both.
branches.cn: 名词与动词同形，一幅画面就够用。

branches.en: A colour can describe a wall or a face.
branches.cn: 颜色既能形容墙面，也能形容面孔。

intro.en: The family grows with -ful, -less, -ing and the prefix dis- to make discoloured.
intro.cn: 这个词族靠 -ful、-less、-ing 与前缀 dis- 构成 discoloured。

latinIntro.en: Color and colare are the Latin sources; the base still means an outward covering.
latinIntro.cn: color 与 colare 是拉丁语来源，词基仍指外在的覆盖。

items.meaning: more than one colour, or he adds colour
items.example: The room uses three warm colours.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间用了三种暖色。

items.meaning: given colour, or having colour
items.example: She wore a brightly coloured scarf.
items.exampleCN: 她戴了一条颜色鲜艳的围巾。

items.meaning: the act of adding colour or a substance that colours
items.example: The sweet contains no artificial colouring.
items.exampleCN: 这种糖果不含人工色素。

items.meaning: full of bright colours or lively detail
items.meaningCN: 色彩丰富的；生动多彩的
items.example: The market was noisy and colourful.
items.exampleCN: 市场喧闹而色彩缤纷。

items.meaning: having no colour or no interest
items.example: The gas is colourless and odourless.
items.exampleCN: 这种气体无色无味。

items.meaning: changed in colour, often for the worse
items.meaningCN: 变色了，通常指变得难看
items.example: The old paper had discoloured at the edges.
items.exampleCN: 旧纸的边缘已经变色。

items.meaning: having many colours
items.example: A multicoloured flag hung above the door.
items.exampleCN: 门上方挂着一面彩色旗。

items.meaning: unable to tell certain colours apart
items.example: He is colour-blind to red and green.
items.exampleCN: 他分不清红色和绿色。

latinEntries.example: Latin color is the direct source of colour.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 color 是 colour 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Colare links colour to the idea of covering.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colare 把 colour 与覆盖的想法连起来。

definition_en: a tall stone post that holds up a building, a regular article in a newspaper, or a line of people or things one behind another
core_image: 一根笔直撑起屋顶的高石柱
scene: 古老的剧院门前立着一排高大的石柱。A white column still stands at the temple gate.
sceneCN: 这里 column 指「柱」（第 1 个义项：支撑建筑的石柱）；句意是神庙门口仍立着一根白色石柱。

senses.title: A supporting post
senses.definition: a tall stone or wooden post that holds up part of a building
senses.definitionCN: 支撑建筑某部分的高石柱或木柱
senses.example: The roof rests on six columns.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶由六根柱子支撑。
senses.why: The Latin word meant the top of a pillar, the part that carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词指柱子的顶端，即承重的部分。

senses.title: A regular newspaper piece
senses.definition: a regular article on one subject in a newspaper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 报刊上关于某一主题的定期文章
senses.example: She writes a weekly column on food.
senses.exampleCN: 她写每周一篇的美食专栏。
senses.why: Print set text in narrow vertical strips, and the page gave the article its name.
senses.whyCN: 印刷把文字排成窄长的竖条，版面便给了这篇文章名字。

senses.title: A line of people or things
senses.definition: a line of people or things standing or arranged one behind another
senses.definitionCN: 人或物前后排成的一列
senses.example: A column of smoke rose from the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 山上升起一柱烟。
senses.why: A pillar is tall and narrow, so anything in a narrow line takes the shape.
senses.whyCN: 柱子又高又窄，于是任何窄长的一列都沿用这个形状。

intro.en: Column comes from Latin columna, a pillar, from columen, the top or summit.
intro.cn: column 出自拉丁语 columna（柱），更早是 columen（顶端、屋脊）。

items.en: Columen meant the top or ridge of a roof.
items.cn: columen 指屋顶的顶端或屋脊。

items.en: Columna named the pillar that held the roof up.
items.cn: columna 指撑起屋顶的柱子。

items.en: French colomne carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 colomne 把词带向英语。

items.en: Printers used column for a vertical strip of text.
items.cn: 印刷者用 column 指竖排的一条文字。

items.en: The word also names a line of troops or of smoke.
items.cn: 这个词也指一列队伍或一道烟。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in spelling, while the meaning group names upright posts and lines.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写相近的词，近义组列出直立的柱与成行之物。

entries.definition: a territory ruled by another country
serious and formal in manner
a book, or the amount of space something fills
entries.definitionCN: 书卷；或某物占的空间量

entries.definition: a tall upright post of stone or wood
entries.definitionCN: 高大的石制或木制立柱

entries.definition: a strong upright piece of wood or metal
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的竖直木柱或金属柱

entries.definition: a line of things placed side by side

normalIntro.en: These hooks stand on the picture of a pillar, then lie down as a strip of print and a line of smoke.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子立在柱子的画面上，再横躺成一条文字与一道烟。

normal.en: Column and colony start alike but grow in different directions.
normal.cn: column 与 colony 开头相似，含义却走向不同方向。

normal.en: The silent n in column comes from the Latin columna.
normal.cn: column 里不发音的 n 来自拉丁语 columna。

normal.en: A pillar holds up a roof, and a printed column holds up a page.
normal.cn: 石柱撑住屋顶，印刷的栏撑住版面。

normal.en: The same tall narrow shape becomes a line of soldiers.
normal.cn: 同一个高而窄的形状变成了行军的队伍。

normal.en: A columnist is the person who fills the column.
normal.cn: columnist 就是填满这个专栏的人。

abstract.en: Picture a temple front of white pillars against blue sky.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝天下一排白色神庙立柱。

abstract.en: Picture one narrow strip of news down a wide page.
abstract.cn: 想象宽大版面上一条窄窄的新闻栏。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line of smoke rising without a bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一道细烟笔直升起。

examples.en: The hall is held up by twelve stone columns.
examples.cn: 大厅由十二根石柱支撑。

examples.en: His column appears in the paper every Friday.
examples.cn: 他的专栏每周五见报。

examples.en: A column of trucks waited at the border.
examples.cn: 一列卡车在边境等候。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 column 记成又高又窄的一条：立起来是石柱，排下去是一列。

root: 源自拉丁语 columna（柱），更早是 columen（顶端、屋脊），后引申为竖排文字、专栏与成列之物。

sensesIntro.en: A tall support first, then a vertical strip of print, and then any narrow line.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是高耸的支撑，再是竖排的一条文字，最后是任何窄长的一列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight tall shape rising from the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个笔直高耸、从地面升起的形状。

branches.en: The stone post is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 石柱义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: Printing turned the tall shape into a strip of text.
branches.cn: 印刷把这个高长形状变成一条文字。

branches.en: Any narrow line borrows the same vertical image.
branches.cn: 任何窄长的一列都借用同一个竖直意象。

branches.en: A pillar and a line of trucks share one narrow shape.
branches.cn: 石柱与车队共享同一个窄长形状。

branches.en: A printed column is itself a line of words.
branches.cn: 印刷的栏本身就是一行行文字排成的列。

intro.en: The family adds -ist for the writer, -ar and -ed for shape, and compounds from daily print.
intro.cn: 这个词族用 -ist 表写作者，用 -ar 与 -ed 表形状，并有日常印刷中的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Columna and columen are the Latin sources, with no prefix needed for the base.
latinIntro.cn: columna 与 columen 是拉丁语来源，词基本身不需前缀。

items.meaning: more than one pillar, column or line
items.meaningCN: 多根柱子、多个专栏或多列
items.example: The table has four columns of numbers.
items.exampleCN: 表格有四列数字。

items.meaning: a writer of a regular newspaper column
items.example: The columnist answered readers every week.
items.exampleCN: 这位专栏作家每周回答读者提问。

items.meaning: shaped like a column
items.example: The rock has a columnar structure.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石呈柱状结构。

items.meaning: having columns
items.example: They entered a columned hall.
items.exampleCN: 他们走进一座有柱的大厅。

items.meaning: a unit measuring printed space
items.example: The advert took two column inches.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告占了两栏英寸。

items.meaning: a newspaper piece about private lives
items.meaningCN: 报道私人生活的报纸栏目
items.example: The gossip column named no one.
items.exampleCN: 这个八卦专栏没有点名。

items.meaning: the line of bones in the back
items.meaningCN: 背部由骨节连成的一列
items.example: The spinal column protects the nerves.
items.exampleCN: 脊柱保护着神经。

items.meaning: the post that holds a car's wheel
items.example: He adjusted the steering column.
items.exampleCN: 他调整了转向柱。

latinEntries.example: Columna is the direct source of column.
latinEntries.exampleCN: columna 是 column 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Columen is the older form behind columna.
latinEntries.exampleCN: columen 是 columna 背后更古老的形式。

definition_en: a tool with teeth for tidying hair, to tidy hair with such a tool, or to search a place very carefully
core_image: 一把齿密的小梳子从发根滑到发梢
scene: 出门前她对着镜子把头发理顺。He combed his hair and straightened his tie.
sceneCN: 这里 comb 指「梳理」（第 2 个义项：用梳子整理头发）；句意是他梳好头发，拉直了领带。

senses.title: A tool for hair
senses.definition: a flat tool with a row of teeth used to tidy hair
senses.definitionCN: 有一排齿、用来理顺头发的扁平工具
senses.example: She keeps a small comb in her pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 她在口袋里放着一把小梳子。
senses.why: The old word named a toothed tool long before it named the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的词先指带齿的工具，很久以后才指动作。

senses.title: To tidy hair
senses.definition: to tidy your hair with a comb
senses.definitionCN: 用梳子把头发理顺
senses.example: He combed his hair before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前他梳了梳头发。
senses.why: The tool became a verb: to work a comb through hair.
senses.whyCN: 工具变成动词：把梳子穿过头发。

senses.title: To search very carefully
senses.definition: to search a place or a set of things thoroughly
senses.definitionCN: 彻底搜遍一个地方或一批东西
senses.example: Police combed the field for clues.
senses.exampleCN: 警察仔细搜查了那片田野寻找线索。
senses.why: A comb's teeth pass through every strand, and a search passes through every corner.
senses.whyCN: 梳齿穿过每根发丝，搜查也穿过每个角落。

intro.en: Comb is a native Germanic word; Old English camb named a toothed tool.
intro.cn: comb 是日耳曼语本族词，古英语 camb 指带齿的工具。

items.en: An old root described a toothed object.
items.cn: 一个古老词根描述带齿的物件。

items.en: Camb named the tool for hair and for weaving.
items.cn: camb 指梳理与织造用的工具。

items.en: The final b was once pronounced, then grew silent.
items.cn: 词尾 b 先发音，后来变得不发音。

items.en: The noun turned into a verb meaning to tidy hair.
items.cn: 名词转为动词，意为梳理头发。

items.en: The verb extended to searching every corner.
items.cn: 动词又扩展到搜遍每个角落。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words near in spelling, while the meaning group names tools and thorough actions.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写相近的短词，近义组列出梳理工具与彻底的动作。

entries.definition: to move toward the speaker or a place
a shape with a round base and a point
entries.definitionCN: 底面为圆、顶端带尖的形状

entries.definition: a grave built of stone
a tool with soft hairs used for tidying
to free hair or thread from knots
entries.definitionCN: 把头发或线从结中解开

entries.definition: to look through a place carefully

normalIntro.en: These hooks run a comb through hair, then stretch the same motion across a whole field.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子让梳子穿过头发，再把同一个动作拉到整片田野上。

normal.en: Comb keeps a silent b, a small trap in spelling.
normal.cn: comb 末尾的 b 不发音，是拼写上的小陷阱。

normal.en: The teeth of a comb explain both tidying and searching.
normal.cn: 梳齿既能说明整理，也能说明搜查。

normal.en: Honeycomb keeps the image of many small cells in a row.
normal.cn: honeycomb 保留了排成一行行小格的形象。

normal.en: Comb your hair is a daily act, comb a field is a police act.
normal.cn: 梳头是日常动作，搜查田野是警察的动作。

normal.en: The tool came first, the verb came later.
normal.cn: 先有工具，后有动词。

abstract.en: Picture a small comb sliding from the forehead to the neck.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小梳子从前额滑到颈后。

abstract.en: Picture many hands parting tall grass in a slow line.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手排成一行，慢慢拨开高草。

abstract.en: Picture a honeycomb full of neat six-sided cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜂巢，满是整齐的六角小格。

examples.en: She always carries a comb in her bag.
examples.cn: 她包里总带着一把梳子。

examples.en: He combed his hair back with water.
examples.cn: 他用水把头发向后梳。

examples.en: Rescuers combed the ruins for survivors.
examples.cn: 救援人员在废墟中仔细搜寻生还者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comb 记成齿密的小梳子：一梳理顺头发，一梳搜遍角落。

root: 日耳曼语本族词，古英语作 camb，本指带齿的梳理工具，后转为梳理与彻底搜查的动作。

sensesIntro.en: A toothed tool first, then the act of tidying, and finally the act of searching every corner.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是带齿的工具，再是整理的动作，最后是搜遍每个角落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of teeth passing through tangled strands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排齿穿过缠结的细丝。

branches.en: The object sense is the oldest in English.
branches.cn: 物件义是英语中最古老的。

branches.en: Tidying is the tool used on hair.
branches.cn: 整理就是把这个工具用在头发上。

branches.en: Searching stretches the same motion over a whole area.
branches.cn: 搜查把同一个动作铺展到整片区域。

branches.en: The noun and the verb share one picture of teeth in hair.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共享齿穿过头发的同一幅画面。

branches.en: Both actions pass through every part without skipping.
branches.cn: 两个动作都逐处穿过，绝不跳过。

intro.en: Comb takes -ing and -er, and joins honey and fine-toothed to build new nouns.
intro.cn: comb 可接 -ing 与 -er，并与 honey、fine-toothed 组合成新名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; comb belongs to the older Germanic layer of English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，comb 属于英语更古老的日耳曼语层。

items.meaning: more than one comb, or he tidies his hair
items.example: The shop sells wooden combs.
items.exampleCN: 这家店卖木梳。

items.meaning: tidied with a comb or searched thoroughly
items.example: The police combed every room.
items.exampleCN: 警察搜查了每个房间。

items.meaning: the act of tidying or searching
items.example: Combing wet hair hurts more.
items.exampleCN: 梳湿头发更疼。

items.meaning: a person or machine that combs fibres
items.example: The comber prepares wool for spinning.
items.exampleCN: 梳毛机为纺线准备羊毛。

items.meaning: not tidied with a comb
items.example: He appeared with uncombed hair.
items.exampleCN: 他头发没梳就出现了。

items.meaning: the wax structure made by bees
items.example: The honeycomb hung from a branch.
items.exampleCN: 蜂巢挂在树枝上。

items.meaning: a comb with teeth set close together
items.example: A fine-toothed comb catches small eggs.
items.exampleCN: 密齿梳能梳下小虫卵。

items.meaning: hair combed across a bare patch
items.example: His comb-over moved in the wind.
items.exampleCN: 他横梳的头发被风吹动。

definition_en: fighting between soldiers or armed groups, or to try hard to stop something harmful
core_image: 两队在尘土中对峙，谁都不肯后退
scene: 士兵在泥泞里训练，一遍遍练习近身格斗。Doctors are working to combat the spread of the disease.
sceneCN: 这里 combat 指「与…作斗争」（第 2 个义项：努力遏止有害事物）；句意是医生们正努力遏制疾病传播。

senses.title: Fighting between forces
senses.definition: fighting between soldiers or armed groups
senses.definitionCN: 士兵或武装团体之间的交战
senses.example: He was wounded in combat.
senses.exampleCN: 他在战斗中受伤。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to strike, because two fighters strike each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为击打，因为两名斗士彼此出手。

senses.title: To fight against something
senses.definition: to try hard to stop or reduce something harmful
senses.definitionCN: 努力阻止或减少有害事物
senses.example: The campaign aims to combat smoking.
senses.exampleCN: 这项运动旨在遏制吸烟。
senses.why: The word moved from fighting people to fighting problems.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从与人作战转向与问题作战。

intro.en: Combat comes from French combattre, from Latin com- together and battuere, to beat.
intro.cn: combat 出自法语 combattre，更早是拉丁语 com-（一起）与 battuere（打击）。

items.en: Battuere meant to beat or strike.
items.cn: battuere 意为打或击。

items.en: Combattuere meant to strike each other.
items.cn: combattuere 意为互相击打。

items.en: Old French combattre named armed fighting.
items.cn: 古法语 combattre 指武装交战。

items.en: English combat named a fight between two sides.
items.cn: 英语 combat 指双方交战。

items.en: The verb now also means to fight a problem.
items.cn: 动词如今还指与问题作斗争。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the comb- shape, while the meaning group names fights and efforts against difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组收的是共享 comb- 形态的词，近义组列出交战与对抗困难。

entries.definition: a tool with teeth for tidying hair
a body in space with a bright tail
to join two things together
a large fight between armies
entries.definitionCN: 军队之间的大规模交战

entries.definition: a hard effort against difficulty
to use force against someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks join com- with the Latin verb for beating, then point the fight at problems.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 com- 与拉丁语的打结合起来，再把战斗指向问题。

normal.en: Com- means together and battuere means beat, so combat is beating together.
normal.cn: com- 意为一起，battuere 意为打，所以 combat 就是打到一处。

normal.en: Combat and battle share the same Latin beating.
normal.cn: combat 与 battle 共享同一个拉丁语打的动作。

normal.en: A combatant is one who fights, a combative person likes to fight.
normal.cn: combatant 是参战者，combative 是爱争斗的人。

normal.en: The verb form is common in news about crime or disease.
normal.cn: 动词形式常见于有关犯罪或疾病的新闻。

normal.en: The noun usually appears in the phrase in combat.
normal.cn: 名词通常出现在 in combat 这个说法里。

abstract.en: Picture two lines of soldiers facing each other in dust.
abstract.cn: 想象两队士兵在尘土中相对而立。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor holding up a chart of falling cases.
abstract.cn: 想象医生举起一张病例下降的图表。

abstract.en: Picture two wrestlers gripping hands and neither giving way.
abstract.cn: 想象两名摔跤手抓住对方，谁也不让。

examples.en: The soldiers trained for close combat in the mud.
examples.cn: 士兵们在泥地里训练近身格斗。

examples.en: New rules aim to combat waste in the city.
examples.cn: 新规定旨在遏制城市中的浪费。

examples.en: She spent her life combating unfair laws.
examples.cn: 她一生都在与不公平的法律作斗争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 combat 记成 com 加 bat：两方一起挥棒，就是打斗。

root: 经法语 combattre 上溯拉丁语 combattuere，com-（一起）加 battuere（打击），由交战引申为对抗有害事物。

sensesIntro.en: First armed men striking each other, then anyone striking back at a harmful force.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是武装者互相击打，再是任何人反击有害的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two forces locked face to face, refusing to step back.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股力量面对面僵持，都不肯后退。

branches.en: The military sense is the oldest and most literal.
branches.cn: 军事义最古老也最字面。

branches.en: The verb sense points the same force at problems.
branches.cn: 动词义把同一股力量指向问题。

branches.en: Both senses need a determined effort against an opponent.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要对对手下坚定的功夫。

branches.en: Campaigns combat crime, waste and disease.
branches.cn: 各类运动都在对抗犯罪、浪费与疾病。

branches.en: The noun lives mostly in fixed phrases such as in combat.
branches.cn: 名词多活在 in combat 这类固定说法中。

intro.en: The family grows with -ant for a fighter, -ive for a temper and compounds from military use.
intro.cn: 这个词族靠 -ant 表参战者、-ive 表性情，以及军事用法中的复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Combattuere and battuere are the Latin sources, and battle keeps the same beating root.
latinIntro.cn: combattuere 与 battuere 是拉丁语来源，battle 保留同一个打击词根。

items.meaning: fights against something harmful
items.example: The program combats hunger in schools.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目对抗校园饥饿问题。

items.meaning: fought against something
items.example: They combated the fire for hours.
items.exampleCN: 他们与大火搏斗了数小时。

items.meaning: fighting against something now
items.example: The team is combating fake news.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队正在对抗虚假信息。

items.meaning: a person who takes part in fighting
items.example: Each combatant wore a red band.
items.exampleCN: 每名参战者都戴红袖标。

items.meaning: ready to argue or fight
items.meaningCN: 随时准备争辩或争斗的
items.example: He gave a combative answer.
items.exampleCN: 他给出了一个火药味十足的回答。

items.meaning: prepared for fighting
items.example: The unit was combat-ready by dawn.
items.exampleCN: 这支部队在天亮前已做好战斗准备。

items.meaning: an area where fighting takes place
items.example: Aid workers entered the combat zone.
items.exampleCN: 援助人员进入了战斗区域。

items.meaning: not involving direct fighting
items.example: He took a non-combat role.
items.exampleCN: 他担任了非战斗岗位。

latinEntries.meaning: to strike each other in fight
latinEntries.example: Combattuere is the source of combat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: combattuere 是 combat 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Battuere also lies behind the word battle.
latinEntries.exampleCN: battuere 也藏在 battle 一词背后。
